intent.quote: We should always work from a clean or managed environment. If there could be a hook that automatically understands what test is connected to what requirement and run them automatically based on stale detection, that would be great. And also of course stale detection should also be a hook and be resolved as soon as possible. I'd rather not run plumb test full if possible and only perform targeted validation as much as possible unless you see an issue with this.
intent.readback: Several agents, worktrees and clones work on one repository at once, kept in step by awareness rather than locks: each line of work shares the intent it has in flight, record files merge field by field, and record ids never collide. A same-field clash or a contradicting capture becomes one intent conflict that you arbitrate through a question. The merge is the one place where unapproved or conflicting intent is held; nothing else stops the work.
will: Share each branch's intent in flight with every other worktree, read-only and cheaply, and tell the agent when another branch changes the same record.
Merge record files field by field, so only a real same-field clash becomes an intent conflict.
Put a contradiction between two lines of work to you as one question (question tool, or the study room when there is more to study), before anything is built when it is caught at capture.
Reserve record ids through a shared git ref and renumber the ones that still collide across clones at the merge, without rewriting history.
Hold a merge, a rebase step or a push, and only those, while touched intent is unapproved, a conflict is open, ids collide, paths are undeclared, links are stale or the log is broken.
wont: Locks, leases, admission or any shared mutable runtime state; a claim is a signal, never a lock.
Transaction machinery, candidate checkouts or a test run at merge time; at push only the covering tests run, and the full suite only when full verification is pending (P10).
Let the agent pick the side of an intent conflict that no recorded intent or answer of yours settles.
Ask you to type a command or name a record id to settle a conflict or approve a merge.
assumptions: A touched requirement counts as approved at the merge when you approved it or the judge cascade validated it against your words (P3, P9); judge approvals are listed in the merge report and you reverse one by saying so.
A new link or a trace exemption added on a branch is approved the same way as a record, never on the agent's word alone.
The quick merge-time check and the pre-push hook are installed when plumb adopts a repository; a hook plumb did not write is left alone.
Settling an intent conflict from an answer you already gave on the same two versions is resolving from recorded intent (P5), not the agent choosing.

requirements.title: Record files merge field by field, and a same-field clash becomes one intent conflict
requirements.statement: plumb's merge driver merges a record file field by field against the merge base, so links, independent fields and examples added on either side merge on their own; an example number added on both sides is renumbered and its links follow, and the driver is declared once however often it is installed. When both sides change the same field differently, the record stays readable, carries one intent conflict holding the base, both versions and their branch labels, and is unconfirmed; every plumb surface shows it once, as that conflict, until it is settled, and a later merge that meets the same record again keeps the open conflict. The owner arbitrates it as P3 says; the chosen version is taken, logged with the owner's words, and the record is confirmed again when that version was; with no judge the question carries no recommendation; then nothing about it remains.

requirements.title: Record ids never collide across worktrees and clones
requirements.statement: Every new record id is reserved through one shared git ref with compare-and-swap, so worktrees of one repository never receive the same id. Ids that still collide across clones are renumbered at the merge: the branch merged into keeps its ids, the incoming record takes a newly reserved id with every reference its side introduced, history is never rewritten, an unchanged record keeps its approval, and the merge check holds any collision left.

requirements.title: Intent in flight is shared, and a contradicting capture is caught before any build
requirements.statement: Each worktree shares the intent it has in flight as a claim in a shared git ref, a signal never a lock, cleared when its branch merges or is deleted, and reads other worktrees read-only and cheaply: under 50 ms with warm caches, no git process for a branch whose tip has not moved, and nothing written in another worktree. The agent is told, one line per record and once per session, when another branch changes a record it works on; nothing is refused or held.

requirements.title: A capture that contradicts another branch's claim is put to the owner before anything is built
requirements.statement: When a capture or direct edit would change a record another branch has claimed, or the judge finds a new requirement contradicts another branch's claim in the same feature, the agent asks the owner one question through the question tool showing both versions by branch, before any record is written, and one early decision that matters is raised once; it outlives the question and is answered by it. A compatible overlap is one warning line. With no judge, or an unsure JEV, the overlap counts as unsure, never as compatible. Until a record matches the owner's answer, the agent is told every turn that it differs and status lists it; a record that changed on main after this branch started is named as such.

requirements.title: The merge is the one hold on unapproved or conflicting intent
requirements.statement: One lightweight merge check runs when git records a merge, rebase, cherry-pick or revert step (quick, no tests) and at push, where the pre-push hook runs the same check with the covering tests and the full suite only when full verification is pending (P10). A merge is held until every touched requirement is approved, by the owner or the judge, at its current hash, no link or exemption added since is unapproved, no intent conflict is open, no ids collide, commits touch only paths their trailers' requirements declare, links are fresh and point at tested files, no affected acceptance test fails or lacks a passing run, and the log is intact. A rebase, cherry-pick or revert step is held while it meets an open intent conflict on a record. The check exits 1 for an undeclared path, a stale or dangling link or a broken log, 5 for a failing or unverified acceptance test and 4 for unapproved or conflicting intent, reporting the first of 1, 5 and 4 that applies; its report fits one screen.

decisions.question: Where is an intent conflict recorded?
decisions.chosen: inside the conflicted record file, as a conflict block with its own IC id

decisions.question: What happens to git's merge when a record has an intent conflict?
decisions.chosen: the merge driver completes, leaving the record unconfirmed with the conflict inside it; the merge check (the quick merge-time hook and the pre-push hook) holds the merge until the conflict is settled
alternatives: the driver stops git's merge until the owner chooses

decisions.question: Which record keeps the id when two clones created the same one?
decisions.chosen: the first parent (the branch merged into) keeps its ids and the incoming record is renumbered
alternatives: the older record keeps its id

retired_decisions.why: a branch-version conflict on SR-184 whose two quoted versions are word-for-word the same; version 2 supersedes SR-184, so the question no longer stands (P5)
a branch-version conflict on SR-182, which version 2 supersedes with the P9 cascade, so the question no longer stands (P5)
a one-time choice about landing the done work under the old record set, not a durable rule; version 2 lands on the owner's word, and afterwards the merge stays the one hold under P11
